summary_en.motivation: To understand the mechanisms of brittleness and anisotropic mechanical properties in H13 steel fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Experimental characterization and microstructural analysis were conducted to correlate processing parameters with mechanical performance.
summary_en.result: The study revealed significant anisotropy in strength and ductility influenced by melt pool boundaries and defects.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing (tensile, hardness) combined with SEM/EBSD microstructural observations.

papers.title: 3D printed scaffolds: Challenges toward developing relevant cellular in vitro models
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) cell culture technology has rapidly emerged, as a result of the increasing demand for improved in vitro systems that better resemble human physiology. Promising microphysiological systems have been fabricated by combining complex 3D culture with 3D-printing technologies. These models overperform existing in vitro systems regarding potential for biofabrication and predictive power. However, most systems under development do not ultimately find a long-term application. We provide herein an overview of the challenges to be considered when developing 3D in vitro systems by means of printed scaffolds, as well as some of the limitations of existing models.

summary_en.motivation: The increasing demand for improved in vitro systems that better mimic human physiology drives the need for 3D cell culture technologies.
summary_en.method: This review provides an overview of challenges and limitations in developing 3D in vitro systems using printed scaffolds.
summary_en.result: It highlights that most systems under development do not find long-term application and identifies key obstacles.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; this is a literature review.
